newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Bayer CEO predicts record profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bayer CEO predicts record profit.

text.p: German chemicals giant Bayer AG will announce a record net profit of over 2.6 billion marks for 1996, raising the prospect of a higher dividend, chief executive Manfred Schneider told the Spiegel news weekly.

"We always wanted to achieve a profit of 2.6 billion marks after tax. If it is a bit more, then we will probably do something for our shareholders," Schneider told Spiegel in an interview issued on Saturday from its Monday edition.

Asked whether that meant the dividend would be increased, he said: "If the supervisory board ... shares our opinion, then I see a good chance. We have always said that we would link our payouts to earnings."
Bayer made a group net profit of 2.4 billion marks in 1995, on which it paid a 15 mark dividend. It announces 1996 results on March 11.
Despite expected profit gains, Schneider said Bayer would not create any new jobs in Germany because of high taxes, high labour overheads and over-regulation.
"These disadvantages have compelled us and will continue to force us to reduce jobs. We will not, for the foreseeable future, create any new jobs in Germany," he told Spiegel.

Investment in Germany, which will total 1.8 billion marks in 1997, will go primarily into rationalisation. Jobs, he said, were too expensive in Germany, with around half the 90 mark hourly cost of a worker consumed by social insurance charges.
